sources.text: A Xbox Game Studios e a Playground Games divulgaram um novo vídeo de gameplay de Fable , reboot da tradicional franquia de RPG. A apresentação aconteceu nesta quinta-feira (12), durante as comemorações dos 25 anos do Xbox , e trouxe aproximadamente quatro minutos de uma missão inédita. O vídeo apresenta uma sequência de exploração na região de Deepwood, onde o protagonista investiga acontecimentos mágicos que estão afetando os moradores de Oakshire. O novo Fable tem lançamento previsto para 23 de fevereiro de 2027 , com versões para PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S e PC. A demonstração acompanha o Herói de Briar Hill, protagonista da aventura, ao lado de Arden, um herói local. Os dois entram nas profundezas de Deepwood para investigar fenômenos mágicos que vêm causando problemas aos habitantes de Oakshire. Durante a missão, os personagens encontram uma área onde a magia natural da floresta parece ter sido corrompida por uma força externa. A exploração também revela pistas sobre quem ou o que pode estar por trás dos acontecimentos, estabelecendo um dos mistérios que os jogadores deverão investigar. Segundo a descrição oficial da Xbox Game Studios, a sequência foi preparada especialmente para as comemorações de aniversário da marca. O material oferece uma nova amostra da ambientação de fantasia do RPG, que marca o retorno de uma das franquias mais conhecidas do Xbox. Desenvolvido pela Playground Games, estúdio responsável pela franquia Forza Horizon , o novo Fable representa um reinício da série de RPG criada originalmente pela Lionhead Studios. O jogo está previsto para chegar em 23 de fevereiro de 2027 , nas seguintes plataformas: A chegada ao PlayStation 5 também amplia a disponibilidade da franquia, historicamente associada aos consoles Xbox. Com a nova demonstração, a Microsoft continua apresentando detalhes do retorno de Fable , que terá uma nova interpretação do universo de fantasia de Albion. sources.name: Kotaku
sources.title: Take-Two CEO Says Discs Will Become Gaming’s Vinyl: ‘It’s Going To Be A Very Small Part Of The Business’
sources.text: Discs GTA 6 Physical Games PlayStation Rockstar Games Vinyl Grand Theft Auto 6 is the first major console game to release without a physical version. Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick doesn’t think it’ll be the last. Physical games will hang around, but not in any mass-market sort of way. He says they’ll become closer to the equivalent of vinyl records in music. âIt may not be the end, but listen, weâve been talking, you and I, for a long time,â he told The Game Business ‘ Christopher Dring in a new interview. âI predicted that digital distribution would be well over 90 percent of the business more than 10 years ago. I donât always get it right, but this one I got right. Will there always be some physical business? Yes, in the same way that thereâs still a vinyl business in recorded music. But itâs going to be a very small part of the business.â Physical music accounted for just over 10 percent of total music revenue in the first half of 2026, according to estimates by theÂ Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA) . That comes out to $581 million, roughly 80 percent of which was earned through sales of vinyl. According to Circana , physical game sales in the U.S. last year hit a 30-year low of $1.5 billion. That was about 2.5 percent of the $60.7 billion consumers spent on âvideo game hardware, content, and accessoriesâ in 2025. Physical game sales are already a smaller chunk of overall game spending than vinyl is for music, and that’s before PlayStation game discs go away entirely in 2028. Game discs becoming vinyl would actually be a rosier outlook than where things currently seem to be trending. We still don’t know how Microsoft will approach physical media with the launch of its Project Helix family of next-gen consoles, and Nintendo has confirmed it has no plans to abandon physical games during the Switch 2 era, even if it’s already taken a half-step in that direction with game key cards. Will GTA 6 ever get a disc version? Vinyl has been a way for music lovers to immortalize their favorite albums. Surely the biggest game launch ever deserves something similar? Zelnick previously shot down rumors that GTA 6 wasn’t coming to disc. He’s now demurred on whether it could get a physical release in the future. That sort of âinformation always comes from our labels,” he told Variety this week, leaving the ball in Rockstar’s court to decide. GTA 6 is getting a vinyl release for its soundtrack , however. Seem a bit hypocritical? It’s probably less surprising when, as revealed in Take-Two’s latest financials, only 2 percent of its current revenue comes from game discs . sources.title: Take-Two boss isn't ruling out a GTA movie or TV show, but says they're "very, very selective" about who they work with
sources.text: A Grand Theft Auto movie could still happen one day With less than a week to go until the release of GTA 6 – aka the biggest entertainment release of all time – the boss of GTA publisher Take-Two isn't ruling out a GTA movie or TV show, but suggests one hasn't happened yet because they're "very, very selective" about who they work with. Speaking on The David Rubenstein Show , Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick was asked why, after 30 years and six mainline games, there still hasn't been a GTA adaptation, saying in response: "We're very careful about line extensions [adaptations in other mediums] because this is a creative company and our goal is to make the best entertainment on Earth. "We would make a movie or a television show based on our IP if our creative teams were passionate about it," Zelnick continued. "If they thought that would somehow engage and delight our consumers. It's a high bar to do that, and of course there's always the risk of failure. So we don't rule it out, but we're very, very selective." Video game adaptations are currently all the rage in Hollywood. 2026 alone saw the release of Resident Evil , Mortal Kombat 2, Street Fighter, Iron Lung, Exit 8, Return to Silent Hill, and the back half of Fallout season 2 , and 2027 looks to be even bigger for video games on screen with The Legend of Zelda movie , A Minecraft Movie 2 , Sonic 4 , and potentially a wave of TV shows set to release. GTA is a unique case, however, and given its scale, it's arguable that Rockstar and Take-Two would have more to lose than gain from a GTA movie or TV show if any adaptation can't live up to the medium-defining legacy of the games. That said, imagine a GTA movie directed by one of the crime movie greats – a Michael Mann or a Martin Scorsese. Could Rockstar resist if one of the legendary filmmakers who informed much of their work wanted to return the favor? For now, the closest we have to a GTA movie is the 2015 docudrama The Gamechangers, which stars Harry Potter's Daniel Radcliffe as then Rockstar Games President Sam Houser and depicts the legal battle with Florida attorney Jack Thompson over the supposed psychological effects of violent games. Rockstar, famously, weren't fans, tweeting : "Was Basil Brush busy? What exactly is this random, made-up bollocks?" As for GTA 6, the map for the long-awaited Vice City-set game just leaked , and it could be teasing a UFO Easter egg. For that and much more, head on over to our countdown to GTA 6 landing page. GTA 6 releases on November 19. For more, check out our list of the best video game movies , and our guide to all the upcoming video game movies and shows heading our way. Subscribe for a weekly digest of the movie and TV news that matters, direct to your inbox. From first-look trailers, interviews, reviews and explainers, we’ve got you covered. In a previous life as a print dinosaur, I was the Deputy Editor of Total Film magazine, and the news editor at SFX magazine. stories.title: The Legend of Zelda Series Was in 'Dire Straights' Before Breath of the Wild, Former Nintendo Marketing Leads Say
stories.summary: The Zelda series was in “dire straits” before Breath of the Wild, with a dwindling playerbase and low sales, according to former Nintendo marketing leads.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: The Legend of Zelda Series Was in 'Dire Straights' Before Breath of the Wild, Former Nintendo Marketing Leads Say
sources.text: The Zelda series was in “dire straits” before Breath of the Wild, with a dwindling playerbase and low sales, according to former Nintendo marketing leads. Kit Ellis and Krysta Yang, who both worked at Nintendo for over a decade, made the claims on the latest episode of their podcast (as spotted by GamesRadar+ ). They refuted the idea that Breath of the Wild ruined the Zelda series with its new formula, and instead argued that it actually saved the franchise from a loss of relevance. It comes as part of a discussion about “new Zelda” versus “old Zelda” — or essentially, the dungeon format versus a complete open world. While there is clearly a demand for the older Zelda games, as evidenced by the hugely successful Ocarina of Time remake, the pair say there is a good reason why Nintendo took them away from us in the first place. “There has been some revisionist history out there lately, about how the Zelda team ripped these away from us at the peak of their popularity,” Ellis says. Yang then expresses her disbelief that fans think this way. “That’s ridiculous. This series was in dire straits. They were selling, like, nothing.” Ellis goes into more detail: “I remember, I was going to the focus groups, and it was a really dark moment when the feedback [was that] the fanbase is dwindling, this is not bringing in new players.” Yang agrees again, saying that it was “depressing,” and that the playerbase was shrinking “smaller and smaller” with each new Zelda release. Before Breath of the Wild came out in 2017, the Zelda series had seen Wii entry Skyward Sword in 2011, A Link Between Worlds in 2013, and various HD and 3D re-releases. Certainly, Breath of the Wild was an enormous hit, selling an incredible 34.28 million copes on the Switch. Its sequel, Tears of the Kingdom, came out in 2023 and has sold 22.90 million so far. The Ocarina of Time remake looks like it continues the positive sales trend , becoming the fastest-selling Switch 2 game so far. The question now is, what will Nintendo do with its inevitable next mainline Zelda game? The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake is out now exclusively on the Nintendo Switch 2. You can read our review of the game here , or check out our look at the Biggest Changes from the original 1998 game. Be sure to check out our expanding Ocarina of Time Remake Walkthrough for comprehensive guides on each main quest area and dungeon, plus where to get Early Heart Pieces, Early Gold Skulltulas , and Early Item Bag Expansions . If you’re looking for more, don’t miss our complete guides to All Pieces of Heart , All Gold Skulltulas , and All Empty Bottles ! Rhiannon (she/her) is a freelance journalist who has been in the industry since 2019. She won MCV's Women in Games award in 2025 and adores RPGs. You can follow her on Bluesky at @rhithewitch.

sources.name: GamesRadar
sources.title: The Legend of Zelda was in "dire straits" before Breath of the Wild, ex-Nintendo marketing leads say
sources.text: The Legend of Zelda might be one of Nintendo's biggest series, but according to two of the company's former marketing leads, it was in "dire straits" before Breath of the Wild, which introduced a massive open-world overhaul that left the franchise's classic formula behind. Last week saw the launch of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time 's Switch 2 remake, which is already an enormous success with 5.2 million copies sold in its first four days. Notably, although it's a remake rather than an entirely new game, it shows there's still a huge appetite for the classic Zelda formula – something that Kit Ellis and Krysta Yang have been discussing in a new episode of their podcast below. Ellis and Yang – former director of social media marketing and original content, and senior manager of creator relations and original content at Nintendo of America, respectively – have been chatting about whether the Ocarina of Time remake could open the door for more traditional Zelda games going forward, as opposed to the Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom-style open-world games which have served as the series' most major releases in the last nine years. While Yang would be interested in a game that combines the classic Zelda-style dungeons with the open-world format, Ellis would "like to see a modern attempt on a classic Zelda game" with that aspect left out entirely. However, this brings him to another point – what he calls "revisionist history" of the series' releases. He calls out fans who've suggested that "the Zelda team ripped these [classic-style games] away from us at the peak of their popularity," prompting Yang to jump in: "That's ridiculous. This series was in dire straits. They were selling, like, nothing." Ellis recalls: "I remember, I was going to the focus groups. It was a really dark moment of like, the feedback is 'the fan base is dwindling, this is not bringing in new players.'" According to him, Nintendo had "so much data" showing that "the interest in the audience was getting smaller and smaller" with every new game. As a result, he says, "They had to do something dramatic like that." Obviously, Breath of the Wild was an enormous success – per Nintendo's data , as of the end of September, the Switch 1 version had sold a whopping 34.28 million copies, with its sequel Tears of the Kingdom coming in with 22.9 million. They're both considered some of the best Zelda games of all time , and for good reason. But, as Ellis and Yang discuss, the Ocarina of Time remake has already proven that folks enjoy the more traditional experiences, too. I don't think we were ever at risk of Zelda going totally open world – even since Breath of the Wild's launch, we've seen the Link's Awakening remake and Echoes of Wisdom, as well as Skyward Sword's HD remaster, giving us new top-down and 3D releases, respectively. Sign up to our Switch 2 Spotlight newsletter to make sure you get the very latest news on Nintendo's new console and its games every week Like Ellis, though, I'd be keen to see a brand new, classic-style 3D Zelda game at some point. After all, not counting remakes, remasters, and ports, the last one was technically 2011's Skyward Sword – it's fair to say we're due for something fresh. Despite GTA 6 being pitted against Zelda: Ocarina of Time, Take-Two boss has nothing but praise – Nintendo "should be proud" as the game is "terrific." I'm GamesRadar+'s Deputy News Editor, working alongside the rest of the news team to deliver cool gaming stories that we love. After spending more hours than I can count filling The University of Sheffield's student newspaper with Pokemon and indie game content, and picking up a degree in Journalism Studies, I started my career at GAMINGbible where I worked as a journalist for over a year and a half. I then became TechRadar Gaming's news writer, where I sourced stories and wrote about all sorts of intriguing topics. In my spare time, you're sure to find me on my Nintendo Switch or PS5 playing through story-driven RPGs like Xenoblade Chronicles and Persona 5 Royal, nuzlocking old Pokemon games, or going for a Victory Royale in Fortnite. sources.name: Polygon
sources.title: Breath of the Wild Saved the Zelda Series From ‘Dire Straits’
sources.text: The open world take seems to have revitalized the series The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time ’s remake is a huge success. Beyond receiving effusive praise from critics , who say this revamp strengthens what made the original one of the best games ever made , it has already sold more than 5.2 million copies , which Nintendo says gives it the "highest global sales for any Nintendo-published Nintendo Switch 2 game in its first four days." It's also the system's highest-selling title after Mario Kart World, which has moved over 16 million copies. The game’s massive popularity has sparked debates about whether Nintendo should pivot away from the open-world formula introduced in Breath of the Wild in favor of the series’ classic dungeon-focused design. Former Nintendo of America director of social media marketing and original content Kit Ellis and senior manager of creator relations and original content Krysta Yang offered some fascinating context on the most recent episode of their podcast. While Ellis says he would be interested in a “modern attempt on a classic Zelda game,” he sheds some light on the state of the series before the release of Breath of the Wild . He rejects the “revisionist history” that “the Zelda team ripped these [traditional Zelda games] away from us at the peak of their popularity.” Yang adds, “This series was in dire straits. They were selling nothing.” Breath of the Wild is the most successful Legend of Zelda game ever, with 34.51 million units sold. The last classic-styled Zelda game was 2011's Skyward Sword , which sold 4.15 million. That was a big drop from the 8.93 million sold for its predecessor, Twilight Princess . “I remember I was going to the focus groups,” Ellis said. “It was a really dark moment. The feedback is ‘the fan base is dwindling; this is not bringing in new players.’” He claims that Nintendo had “so much data” that “the interest in the audience was getting smaller and smaller” and the company “had to do something dramatic” in response. While The Legend of Zelda clearly needed a revamp after Skyward Sword , Ocarina of Time ’s success shows there are still many fans looking for more traditional, dungeon-focused games. Perhaps the remake's impressive buzz will lead to a new classic-style Zelda game, or at least bring more elements of this approach into the next major title.

sources.name: GamesIndustry.biz
sources.title: CD Projekt Red used AI to alter the voice of Geralt's original Polish actor in Witcher 3: Songs of the Past
sources.text: Localisation producer described use of AI as a "special case" after a stroke caused Jacek Rozenek's voice to change when returning for new expansion For The Witcher 3's Songs of the Past expansion, CD Projekt Red used AI to alter the voice of Geralt's original Polish actor, Jacek Rozenek. In 2019, Rozenek suffered a stroke that left him unable to speak. In an interview with Game File , he described his recovery, which required six to seven hours of voice training daily. Rozenek briefly returned to voice Geralt in The Witcher 3's 2022 next-gen update but found the sessions exhausting. CDPR wanted him back for Songs of the Past but recognised his voice now differs significantly from 12 years ago. "For future projects, when we consider Geralt is becoming older and has a deeper voice, this is not a problem for us at all," said CDPR's localisation producer Mikołaj Szwed. "It's more about this specific situation here, where we have both the voice from 12 years ago and from now next to each other, which could kind of take people out of the experience and feel that like there is this difference." "Because, when you listen to the voice from Jacek, it's still Geralt, but when you compare it to Geralt from 12 years ago, Jacek's voice now is much lower, much gruffer." CDPR approached Ukrainian AI company Respeecher to adjust Rozenek's voice, with the actor's consent. "The point is that this voice should be as close as possible to my voice from 12 years ago," Rozenek said. "I have great trust [...] for the creators of this game." CDPR previously worked with Respeecher to recreate the voice of Polish voice actor Miłogost 'Miłek' Reczek, who voiced Viktor Vektor in Cyberpunk 2077, following his death in 2021 with the family's consent. In this case, Respeecher's AI was trained on Rozenek's 2014 recordings to adjust his current voice to match his younger self. "We basically delivered to Respeecher all the lines that Jacek recorded for us for The Witcher 3," Szwed said. "They created an algorithm of his voice, based on his lines." "Getting there took dozens of hours, training models, going through the details with the CDPR team, and dealing with AI artefacts that never fully disappear," said Respeecher synthetic speech artist Dmytro Vasylets. "The hardest part was Jacek's emotional range: the half-tones, shouts, groans, anger, fear and laughter. Capturing all of that at the highest audio quality was the real challenge. I'd like to think we pulled it off." Szwed said CDPR's contracts confirm that they would not use any actors' voices with AI without the actor's consent. "I do think this is one of those ways where you can use AI ethically, with consent and also to do something good," Szwed said. "This was a special case." The use of generative AI in voice acting remains a strong topic of debate. Last month, the Japan Actors' Union announced new guidelines for the unauthorised use of generative AI to replicate voices. One stipulation is that if generative AI replicates a performance, it must be treated as a new performance and require additional royalties or compensation. UKIE also announced a partnership with law firm Sheridans to offer an AI Compliance and Accreditation Service , supporting UK studios in using AI lawfully and responsibly.

God of War: Sons of Sparta first launched for PlayStation 5 on February 12, 2026. The free content update introduces two new game modes, which can be selected upon starting a new game and selecting a save slot. Once selected, the game mode chosen for that save file cannot be changed. The new modes are as followed: Here is an overview of the game, via Sony Interactive Entertainment: Join young Kratos and Deimos, sons of Sparta, on a Greek odyssey as they discover the meaning of duty and honor. Every legend has a beginning—before he was a God, before he was a father, Kratos was a young Spartan! Experience an untold chapter in Kratos’ journey set during the harsh years of Spartan training alongside his brother Deimos. Through endless trials, their minds, bodies, and hearts have been molded to become Spartan soldiers for whom duty and honor mean everything. After a fellow cadet goes missing, Kratos and Deimos vow to find him and embark on an adventure that will put their training and Spartan spirit to the test. Guide Kratos and Deimos through vibrant and varied 2D levels that will test your combat prowess and cleverness as you search for their missing friend. Solve environmental puzzles, face down enemies both new and familiar, and topple mythological bosses that will test the limits of your Spartan training. Through adversity and cooperation, they’ll learn what it means to be a true Spartan, brother, and friend. An engaging and exciting 2D action-adventure brought to life from the talented pixel superstars at Mega Cat Studios. Experience retro classic gameplay with God of War ‘s signature spectacle, action, and heartfelt storytelling.

sources.title: God of War: Sons of Sparta Gets PS4 Release and Two New Game Modes
sources.text: The prequel to God of War, God of War: Sons of Sparta is a 2D metroidvania that sets the scene for the series. The game has been available on the PlayStation 5 since February 2026. However, it is just now coming out for PlayStation 4 on November 16. To celebrate the game becoming available to even more players, Santa Monica Studio and Mega Cat Studios are releasing two more modes that will be playable on both consoles. The new Hermes mode for God of War: Sons of Sparta is unlocked after the game has been completed. Players get special tools to see how quickly the game can be accomplished in this speedrun mode. Erebus mode is available at any point of the game. It takes out both the player and the enemy in one hit. Players will need to avoid taking any damage to avoid death. These new modes could give God of War fans something to enjoy while they wait for the release of God of War Laufey . Santa Monica Studio recently announced their choice to delay God of War Laufey . It is arriving in May 2027, three months after the initial release date of February 2027. What are your thoughts on God of War: Sons of Sparta’s new modes?
